note: The first R-VES reading this repository has taken, the floor it has to be read against, and the correction of the explanation a previous round published for the gap. `eval/bird/ves.ts` implements the metric (tau = time(gold)/time(predicted), bands 1.25/1/0.75/0.5/0.25, 0 for a wrong answer), `eval/bird/oracle.py` reports the microsecond clock it needs, and both are tested. The run is over the 600-question dev artifact this repository already held — `eval/out/bird-eval-41453395203.json`, run 41453395203, arm `select-cross`, 378 correct of 600 (63.0%) — because the only full-dev artifact is inside a GitHub Actions run whose logs and artifacts this sandbox cannot retrieve (the signed URL answers 401). The number is therefore a coordinate on the metric and not the leaderboard row: the leaderboard files OpenSearch-SQL at 69.36 over all 1,532 questions, and a rate over 600 of them is a different claim. THE FLOOR: timing every correct statement against itself — the same two blocks of five executions, gold on both sides — reads 57.96%, with 121 of the 378 correct answers landing in the 0.75 band and none in the 1.25 band. That is not a statement's speed: it is the reward table's step at tau = 1, which pays a quarter less for a ratio that is a hair below one and does not pay more until a ratio of two, plus a stopwatch that cannot resolve 544 microseconds (the corpus median) to better than about one percent. So of the 6.37pp that separate EX (63.0) from R-VES (56.63), 5.04pp are the harness's own floor and 1.33pp are the statements. THE CORRECTION: a previous round attributed the 6.2pp gap to the joins and subqueries this harness ships that the gold does not. Both halves of that were measured and both are false. Of the 145 statements in the 0.75 band, 131 carry exactly the same number of joins as their gold query, 9 carry more and 2 fewer; the same holds for subqueries (6 more, 5 fewer) and every other shape dimension, and a per-dimension cross-tabulation puts the median tau of the cases carrying an extra join at 0.86 — inside the floor's own spread. The claim was a plausible story checked against nothing, and it is replaced by the floor, which is the same measurement the reading already makes, on a case list whose predictions are their own gold.
trim: median absolute deviation, x3; fewer than three samples takes the fastest
normalization: mean over all scored questions; `rvesOfValid` is the same reward divided by the 378 answers that were right

bands.label: between a quarter and a half

floor.note: `--self-check` replaces every prediction with its gold statement and runs the same measurement again. The 5.04pp it costs is arithmetic, not luck: 121 * 0.25 / 600. A noise band that is symmetric around one would lose nothing if the table were symmetric, and this one is not — the step above 1 is at 2. The same floor applies to every system measured by this harness on this corpus, including the rows on the leaderboard, which is why the distance between EX and R-VES there is 2.92pp for the top row and 6.37pp here.
